A four-column table charting episodes from Star Wars and The Empire Strikes Back in the manner of Lévi-Strauss’s analysis of the Oedipus myth. The columns are headed “Overrating of kinship,” “Underrating of kinship,” “The living defeat the machine,” and “The machine persists in the body.” Most rows hold a single episode in one column, so the rows run in narrative order while the columns group episodes by meaning. In order: Luke’s father thought dead (underrating kinship), sharing a row with Anakin Skywalker breathes only with prosthetic assistance (machine persists in the body); Owen keeps Luke on the farm (overrating kinship); Owen and Beru are incinerated (underrating kinship); Obi-Wan severs an arm in the cantina (machine persists in the body); Vader tortures Leia, unaware she is his daughter (underrating kinship); Luke rescues Leia (overrating kinship); Vader kills Obi-Wan, the substitute father (underrating kinship); Luke turns off his targeting computer and destroys the Death Star (the living defeat the machine); Luke severs the wampa’s arm (machine persists in the body); Luke trips an AT-AT with a cable (the living defeat the machine); Leia kisses Luke (overrating kinship).

SSA is the nation's largest and most trusted government service provider, safeguarding information and delivering service to more than 330 million Americans with active Social Security numbers. Over the past year, we have accelerated our digital-first strategy, streamlined our operations, and focused our resources to improve your experience whether you choose to interact with us online, by phone, by video, or in person.

Fiscal year (FY) 2026 produced the best performance in the agency’s 91-year history. We reduced average wait times on our National 800 Number to under six minutes, an 80 percent improvement compared to FY 2024. We cut average field office wait times by more than 30 percent while serving nearly 30 million visitors in our over 1,200 field offices. Americans completed more than 571 million online transactions during the year, and more than 105 million people now have a personal my Social Security account. We also reduced disability processing times and backlogs, helping the most vulnerable receive decisions more quickly.
